what: Twist Bioscience makes synthetic DNA. It prints genes on silicon chips rather than in plastic tubes, which makes DNA far cheaper, and sells it to researchers, drug developers and diagnostic companies.
customers: Pharmaceutical and biotech researchers, diagnostics companies, and academic laboratories.
moat: Silicon-based DNA synthesis that no competitor has matched at the same cost per base, which is the entire reason customers buy from it.
risks: A $130M net loss and negative free cash flow
17 times sales for a company that does not yet make money
Academic and biotech research budgets have been tight
opportunities: Revenue grew from $204M to $459M in four years, and it has not stopped growing through the downturn
Analysts see about 15% upside, and DNA data storage would be an entirely new market for the same technology
watch: Revenue growth and the path to positive cash flow.
